known_staging_gaps: Outbound mail RESOLVED 2026-08-08T18:07Z. It was never a permissions gap and never a code gap: a token probe inside the container showed roles=["Mail.Send"], and the refusal carried graph_error_code=ErrorAccessDenied, which is Exchange's application access policy rather than Entra. The policy was created 07:13Z and began enforcing between 07:54Z (last refusal) and 18:07Z (first success). Test-ApplicationAccessPolicy reported Granted the whole time because it evaluates configured state, not enforced state -- worth remembering before trusting it again.

schema.note: This is a log of what has been OBSERVED applied via apply-migrations run output, not a generated schema version. Every pilot:apply-* runner is additive/idempotent, so re-running one is safe -- this list exists to avoid re-running unnecessarily, not to gate anything. Added 2026-08-10: entries here record what a RUNNER reported, which is weaker than reading the schema back. A green apply-migrations run proves each runner's own readiness assertion passed -- and the drills incident showed a readiness assertion can itself be wrong, so a gatekeeper checking a specific object should still query for it rather than trust this list.

runtime_verified: magic-link redemption on staging: POST /api/pilot/auth/magic-link/consume returns 200 and sets ppbf_pilot_session for the correct principal; the same token replayed returns TOKEN_ALREADY_USED; GET returns 405 with Allow: POST so a mail scanner's prefetch cannot burn a link; exactly one session row created (2026-08-08, staging)

magic-link DELIVERY on staging, the whole chain with a human in it (2026-08-08T18:07-18:12Z): request answered 202 and wrote a token row; no magic_link.issue_failed line on a warm container; the mail arrived in a real mailbox; the owner clicked it; consumed_at 18:12:51.064Z. Silence alone would not have proved this -- issueMagicLink is deliberately silent for an unknown address too -- so the token row was read back to separate 'sent' from 'no such account'.

magic-link single-transaction claim: the session row's created_at is 18:12:51.064Z, identical to the token's consumed_at, confirming the claim and the session insert happen in one transaction rather than two writes that could interleave. Exactly one session for that account from that click, and the only other session in the window belongs to a Microsoft sign-in by the owner.

magic-link supersession: every older token row carries invalidated_at set by the request that followed it, and no two were ever live at once -- so requesting a second link genuinely kills the first rather than leaving both valid.

T-003 quarantined-video scan-review console (2026-08-08, retroactive). Acceptance criteria: page.test.tsx 5/5 including a WrongRoleNotice case for a non-deciding role and separate approve and block cases. Role gate proven against the DEPLOYED app, not only against mocks: a real coach session returns 403 'Forbidden: role not allowed' on POST /api/pilot/video/scan-review, which is the ticket's P0 rule (the coach who filmed footage of a minor gets no path into the decision). A real platform_owner session is refused identically -- VIDEO_REVIEW_DECIDE_ROLES is ['organization_admin'] and nothing else, so even the platform owner cannot decide. Unauthenticated, video/list, review-link and scan-review all answer 401 on BOTH environments and /admin/video-review renders 200. Production has 4 active organization_admin accounts, so the console is usable by someone. Probe sessions were minted on staging only and deleted in a finally block; 0 remained. No session was minted on production and no real video was approved or blocked anywhere.
